messages:
maria: Quick update — canary for the shared-allocator + dynamic-KV-prune change finished. Results look good: p99 latency down ~18% and per-token cost down ~22% on the production mix. Rolling to 80% traffic now :tada:

maria: TL;DR numbers (prod mix, avg across 6 nodes):
```text
Before: p50=24ms, p95=98ms, p99=240ms, cost/token=$0.00128
After:  p50=26ms, p95=83ms, p99=197ms, cost/token=$0.00099
GPU util avg: 62% -> 57% (less tail thrash)
KV-cache hitrate (prefix cache): 31% -> 44%
CPU sys% drop ~6pts on worker-side batching
```

kevin: awesome. any error-rate bumps or decoding regressions? did we see more truncation / early-exit for long prompts?

maria: no error-rate regression in the canary (5h window). 500-levels stable, client-side retries unchanged. small uptick in early-exit for sequences > 3k tokens but quality evals show no meaningful semantic degradation — likely due to slightly different microbatch scheduling. we have a follow-up perf-quality eval in the pipeline.

sanjay: curious about long-context chat workloads — what's p99 for >4k tokens specifically?

maria: for >4k contexts (subset of traffic): p99 went from ~720ms -> ~610ms. cost/token savings actually higher on those flows because dyn-prune evicts cold KV frames earlier and reduces KV memory pressure.

tara: do we need to notify customers / change wording in release notes? any known customers using fallback-sensitive configs?

maria: flagging @support and account leads for a heads up. no customer-facing behavior changes expected; this is an internal scheduling + pruning optimization. still, we'll add a short note in the console release banner and the changelog: "Runtime: improved latency and cost via shared allocator + KV pruning".

kevin: what's the rollout plan / guardrails? can we rollback quickly if algo misbehaves?

maria: rollout plan: 0->canary(5%) -> 5% -> 20% -> 80% (now) -> 100% if stable. holding at 80% for 60m to validate cross-region traffic. rollback is a single flip in the runtime feature-flag store (console UI + infra API). metric gates: >2% p99 regression OR error-rate up >0.5% triggers auto-rollback. oncall is already subscribed to the alert channel.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment complete: commit sha=ab3f9e4 -> promoted to 80% on prod cluster. Monitoring: perf-gates OK, error-rate OK. (link: https://redwood.internal/deploys/ab3f9e4)

sanjay: nice. can we also capture a short benchmark microreport for the eng wiki? want the perf curves per seq-len bins to use in modeling.

maria: yup — I'll dump the per-bin numbers and attach to the PR, plus a Grafana dashboard snapshot. planning a short post in #eng-runtime with the bench graphs and a runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-prune-deploy

kevin: shout if you want me to hold the 100% step and run a manual smoke for the top 10 customers.

maria: thanks — will ask if we see anything odd after the 60m window. big thanks to the perf/infra teams for squeezing the tail and the billing folks for the cost model check :heart:

tara: :clap: great win. can we add a one-paragraph exec blurb for Friday all-hands?

maria: on it, will DM you a short blurb and the numbers.

kevin: reaction :thumbsup:

maria: tagging follow-ups: @sanjay for modeling, @kevin infra rollout ops, @tara comms. closing notes will be posted in #eng-runtime after 100% or rollback.

(automated note) metrics collected: p50/p95/p99, cost/token, kv-hit, gpu-util, error-rate. thresholds defined in the runbook.
